newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity called lower, extends Wed. slump.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity called lower, extends Wed. slump.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were called to open sharply lower Thursday, continuing Wednesday's retreat from the recent spike on easing physical power prices due to cooler weather in parts of the Southwest.
"We're seeing it crash this morning," said a West Coast electricity trader, referring much lower prices in over-the-counter (OTC) activity.

June California-Oregon Border (COB) futures, in OTC trading, were quoted at $18.75-19.25 a megawatt hour (MWh) versus Wednesday's settlement at $21.06, while June Palo Verde (PV) at $25.25-25.75 against yesterday's close at $27.68.
Further weakness in the daily market would trigger another drop in futures prices, market sources said.
Day-ahead spot power values in the West were off three to four dollars from Wednesday's levels, traders said.
Stronger natural gas prices could cushion a drop in power prices, brokers and traders said.
"We'll see a bottom if gas opens up," said the West Coast dealer, adding a decline in gas prices would worsen the slump in electricity futures.
NYMEX June Henry Hub natgas futures opened down 1.1 cent at $2.195 per million British thermal units.
Separately, Bonneville Power Administration said the DC lines on the Pacific Intertie will be reduced by as much as 414 megawatts (MW) this week for scheduled maintenance.
At least 7,000 MW of power remained off line in the West for either planned or unplanned maintenance, although a much of the capacity was expected to return to operation over the next several weeks.

As part of the service resumptions, Pacific Gas & Electric's 1,087 MW Diablo Canyon 1 was scheduled to begin production by early next week after completing a scheduled refueling and maintenance outage which began April 19.
Weather Services Corp said conditions in the Northwest would remain warm and wet through next week with main cities like Portand and Seattle seeing readings in the 60s F.

In the Southwest, temperatures would average near normal in the eastern section and above normal in the western area. The California coast is predicted to continue enjoying readings in the 70s, while interior cities like Phoenix and Las Vegas would still experience temperatures in the 90s.
